subject: PWD-1
reason: Council (testPlan, blockOn any, pass 9/10): not passed; opus 9/10, sol 8/10; 2 finding(s) stand, 2 note(s).

items.reason: TC-PWD-1-10 already changes a password and proves the new credential works in a fresh browser context. Delete TC-PWD-1-04; its different valid password adds no branch or unique assertion.

The index identifies lowercase as required, but TC-PWD-1-08 supplies lowercase and no case rejects its absence. Add a password satisfying all other rules but lacking lowercase; assert Identity's lowercase-rule message and unchanged credentials.

Step 2 says 'hover or click the user icon if it opens anything'. For an anonymous visitor the icon is a plain link to the Identity login page, so clicking it leaves the WebApp and the expected results (no 'Change password', sign-in entry in the header) would be evaluated on the wrong page. The step should say: do not click; assert on the rendered WebApp header that the anonymous user icon is the 'Sign in' link and that no 'Change password' element or link exists.

The plan explicitly excludes acceptance at exactly 100 characters. Rejection at 101 and acceptance at 6 cannot detect an incorrectly restrictive upper limit. Add a valid 100-character password change and verify fresh sign-in succeeds.
items.notUpheld: evidence or nothing (rule 4): no file and line, command output or screenshot backs it; it is a question, not a blocking finding

reason: The change page limits only the New password input to 100 characters, so a 101-character password typed into both boxes is reported as a mismatch instead of a length error.

items.expected: After submitting current Factoryfake1$ and the same 101-character value (Factoryfake1$ + 88 'a') in New and Confirm, the page stays on /Manage/ChangePassword and shows 'The New password must be at least 6 and at max 100 characters long.'
items.actual: The page stays on /Manage/ChangePassword but shows only 'The new password and confirmation password do not match.' (in the summary and under Confirm). No length message is shown. The rendered NewPassword input has maxlength="100", so the browser keeps 100 of the 101 characters, while ConfirmPassword has no maxlength and keeps 101.
items.location: src/Identity.API/Views/Manage/ChangePassword.cshtml (NewPassword input rendered by asp-for with the [StringLength(100)] rule from Models/ManageViewModels/ChangePasswordViewModel.cs, which emits maxlength=100; the ConfirmPassword input has no maxlength)
items.reason: The shopper typed the same password twice and is told the entries differ. AC4 requires the page to show what is actually wrong. Because only one of the two inputs is limited, the length error the view model defines can never be shown for input typed into the form.
